analysis.title: China: Recovery stalls, risks rise
key_insights: October industrial production slowed to 4.8% oya from 5.5% in September, below the 5.3% that J.P. Morgan and consensus expected. JPM estimates output fell 0.3% m/m sa.

High-tech manufacturing and electronics output grew 17.6% oya and 19.4%, and industrial robots, integrated circuits and NEVs rose 26.0%, 21.9% and 17.1%. Auto manufacturing slowed to 0.9%, so tech strength has not lifted domestic-demand-sensitive industries.
Fixed asset investment is the clearest drag. JPM estimates October FAI fell 16.1% oya versus 7.2% in September. Official ytd FAI declined 8.1% oya against JPM at -7.1% and consensus at -7.0%.

The investment weakness extends beyond property. Infrastructure FAI is down 5.1% oya ytd and manufacturing FAI down 2.9%, alongside a 21.6% ytd property-investment contraction. Computer and electronics equipment investment grew 12.0%.

Housing remains a drag. New-property sales by floor space fell 13.7% oya ytd and developer funding fell 21.9%. Stronger secondary-market turnover supports transactions but does less for developer cash flow.

Retail sales slowed to 0.4% oya from 1.1%, below JPM's 0.7% and consensus 0.8%. JPM estimates a 0.2% m/m sa decline. Auto retail sales contracted 21.4% oya and communications-equipment sales growth slowed to 6.5% from 31.1%.
Services retail sales rose 4.9% oya ytd versus 0.9% for goods. They have not yet produced a broad spending recovery.
Financing has not turned into demand. October bank loans contracted CNY 100 billion, including a CNY 430 billion fall in household loans. Loan growth slowed to 4.7% oya while TSF growth was 7.2%.

The CNY 800 billion policy-bank funding deployment still has to become spending. Local matching funds and procurement constrain execution. Private, road and public-facilities investment fell 11.4%, 10.9% and 14.1% oya ytd, which points to limited crowding-in.
JPM's baseline is 5.3% q/q saar growth in both 4Q26 and 1Q27 and 4.6% y/y for 2026. It requires fiscal catch-up and sustained tech demand. Execution delays could push support into early 2027.

October headline and core CPI were 0.7% oya and 0.8% against PPI of 5.7%. JPM reads this as upstream cost pressure, not demand-led reflation, and keeps its 2026 CPI forecast at 0.8%. The next rate cut is now expected in 2027.
October exports rose 35.2% oya in US-dollar terms and the surplus narrowed to US$105.3 billion. External resilience is a cushion but not a secure growth engine.

Incoming Democratic control of both US chambers could raise tariff-relief pressure while increasing scrutiny of China, chips and sensitive transactions. Leaders' talks at the APEC summit on November 19 are the next test before the January 10 truce expiry. Compromises would not unwind Section 301 and 232 measures or tech controls.
JPM says risks tilt down. A self-sustaining recovery requires implemented external relief and faster domestic spending.

sector_views.rationale: High-tech manufacturing IP grew 17.6% oya and electronics 19.4%, but this has not broadened to the rest of the economy.
Property investment fell 21.6% oya ytd, new-property sales by floor space fell 13.7% and developer funding fell 21.9%.
Auto retail sales fell 21.4% oya and auto manufacturing output slowed to 0.9%.

risk_factors: Housing weakness continues to depress construction and confidence.
Delays in fiscal execution, including local matching funds and procurement, could weaken transmission of policy-bank funding.
Household loans contracted CNY 430 billion in October, so credit is not turning into demand.
Tariff and tech barriers remain even if the APEC summit eases tensions, and the truce expires January 10.
Tech demand must be sustained for the growth baseline to hold.
geopolitical: Leaders' talks at the APEC summit on November 19 are the next test before the January 10 US-China truce expiry.
Incoming Democratic control of both US chambers could increase tariff-relief pressure while intensifying scrutiny of China, chips and other sensitive transactions.
Compromises could reduce disruption but would not unwind Section 301 and Section 232 measures or tech controls.

tension_points.bull_case: High-tech manufacturing IP grew 17.6% oya, electronics 19.4%, and exports rose 35.2% oya, which cushions output.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech strength has not revived domestic demand. FAI fell 8.1% ytd, retail sales grew 0.4%, and household loans fell CNY 430 billion in October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fiscal delivery falling short of the baseline. JPM's 5.3% q/q saar growth in 4Q26 and 1Q27 requires fiscal catch-up and sustained tech demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Leaders' talks at the APEC summit on November 19 could produce compromises that reduce disruption and protect trade.
tension_points.bear_case: Compromises would not unwind Section 301 and 232 measures or tech controls, and incoming Democratic control of both US chambers could intensify scrutiny of China, chips and sensitive transactions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No agreement at the November 19 APEC talks, or no extension by the January 10 truce expiry.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech resilience has not revived domestic demand, and housing and weak fiscal execution keep the risks tilted down.
